key_insight: Variable-geometry sample-based quantum diagonalization (VGSQD) reuses quantum samples across molecular geometries to reduce quantum computation for geometry optimization and reaction-path calculations.
engineering_relevance: Extending quantum chemistry from fixed-geometry energies to molecular structures and reaction barriers supports workflows relevant to catalysis and drug discovery.
method: Collect quantum samples at a reference molecular geometry.
Reuse those samples in SQD calculations at displaced geometries.
Optimize molecular structures and map reaction energy pathways.
evidence_signal: Using circuits of up to 124 qubits on IBM's ibm-quebec Heron r2 processor, the authors evaluated beryllium dimer and water equilibrium properties and a hydrogen-exchange reaction pathway, reporting results comparable to CCSD(T) and DMRG.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify cost savings or establish how reliably reference samples transfer across larger geometry changes and broader chemical systems.
paper_title: Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization for Variable Molecular Geometries
